newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's Oro Verde hotels eyes expansion.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's Oro Verde hotels eyes expansion.

text.p: Ecuador's Oro Verde hotel chain plans a Latin American expansion including hotels in Colombia, Chile and Venezuela, a company official said.

"Our sights are set on Colombia, Venezuela and Chile because when you have a chain of hotels, it's good to keep them close to each other," Max Dahinden, manager of Oro Verde's Quito hotel, told Reuters in an interview.
He said the chain aims to attract the same tourists as they travel through different Andean countries.
In Ecuador Oro Verde has two five star hotels in Quito and Guayaquil and lower grade establishments in Cuenca and Machala. It plans to spend $15 million opening a fifth hotel in 1997, in Manta.

The firm recently took its first step outside Ecuador when it opened a $34-million five-star hotel in Lima, Peru. Oro Verde plans to build a second Peruvian hotel in the Andean city of Cuzco, one of the country's main tourist attractions.
Dahinden said that it will wait until hotel-building booms in Chile and Colombia die down before making its own entry to those markets.
"I think Venezuela presents the most promising market for a new hotel, because there have not been new developments in the hotel industry recently," he said.
Oro Verde, which is 80-percent Ecuadorean owned, has assets worth $90 million in Ecuador. Its foreign shareholders include Switzerland's Schmidheini family.
Dahinden declined to reveal the chain's profits.

He said that he thought Ecuador's future tourist development would depend on the construction of new airports in Quito and Guayaquil and on an upcoming bill to encourage foreign investment in the industry.
But local industry sources say that the Hilton Hotels Corp and Marriott International Inc hotel chains plan to set up shop in Ecuador in 1997.
